question: Your structured data extraction system serves two workloads. An accounts-payable clerk uploads one invoice and waits on screen for the extracted fields before approving the payment. Separately, every Friday evening the system re-extracts 40,000 archived contracts for a compliance report that is due on Monday morning. Which API choices should you make for these workloads?

options.text: Route the clerk's invoice requests through the Message Batches API for the 50% cost savings, since most batches finish well within an hour.
options.reason: The batch API has no guaranteed latency SLA, so it is inappropriate for a blocking workflow, whatever the typical completion time.

options.text: Route the clerk's invoice requests through the Message Batches API and have the clerk's screen poll for completion, using custom_id to match each result.
options.reason: custom_id only correlates requests with responses; polling cannot remove the up-to-24-hour window, so the blocking workflow still needs the synchronous API.

options.text: Route both workloads through the synchronous API, so that the weekly report and the clerk's invoices share one consistent processing path.
options.reason: The weekly job is non-blocking and latency-tolerant, so the synchronous API gives up the batch API's 50% savings with no benefit.

options.text: Route the weekly archive re-extraction through the Message Batches API, because the report can wait up to 24 hours for results.
options.reason: The Friday-to-Monday job is latency-tolerant, so the batch API fits and gives 50% cost savings within its 24-hour window.

options.text: Route the clerk's invoice requests through the synchronous API, because the clerk cannot continue until the extracted fields return.
options.reason: The clerk's workflow is blocking, and the guide matches blocking workflows to the synchronous API.
